walkthroughs.body_html: Formation requires: sea surface temperatures >26.5degC to depth ~50m; latitude 5-20deg (Coriolis effect non-zero); low wind shear; atmospheric instability; pre-existing disturbance. Warm ocean evaporates, water vapour rises, condenses, releasing latent heat (~2.5 MJ/kg) that drives convection. Coriolis spins the system anti-clockwise (NH). A mature cyclone may release energy equivalent to 200x global electricity generation per day.

Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda) made landfall on 8 November 2013 over Leyte, Philippines, with sustained winds of 315 km/h (Category 5), among the strongest ever measured. A storm surge of ~5-6 m devastated Tacloban City. Death toll: ~6,300; missing: ~1,000; displaced: ~4.1 million; damage: ~$5.8bn. The Philippines, on the western Pacific typhoon belt, faces ~20 cyclones annually; vulnerability is amplified by poverty and coastal exposure.

Immediate response was hampered by destroyed infrastructure (Tacloban airport, roads). International aid included UK (£77m), US ($86m), and the UN OCHA appeal. The Philippine government's Build Back Better programme aimed for resilient relocation but progressed slowly: by 2018 only ~30% of permanent housing was complete. Climate change is projected to increase Category 4-5 frequency by ~10-15% per degree of warming, raising long-term exposure.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.

mcqs.q: What are the three cells of global atmospheric circulation?
options: There is one big Hadley cell from the equator to each pole.
The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
The Hadley cell (equator to 30 degrees), Ferrel cell (30 to 60 degrees) and Polar cell (60 degrees to poles) together redistribute heat from equator to poles.
